title: Opening, Activation and the Funding Window for Savings and Money Market Accounts
content:
### 1. Opening

An account of Savings & Money Market Accounts opens in applied status, with a zero balance and no automatic transfer on record.

### 2. Age at opening

The customer's age in whole years on the opening date, taken from the date of birth carried on the customer profile, must be at least the youngest age to open set for the tier. The profile is the authority for the date of birth; the age the customer gives is not.

### 3. Checking holding at opening

For a tier whose required checking list is not none, the customer must already hold an active checking account of one of the listed tiers on the opening date. The holding is read from the bank's record of the customer's Personal Checking accounts on that date.

### 4. Activation

The account becomes active on the business day its first deposit posts, provided that deposit is at least the minimum opening deposit set for the tier. A smaller first deposit is returned and does not activate the account.

### 5. The funding window

An account still in applied status is closed as unfunded once 30 calendar days have passed after the account was opened. Calendar days are counted with the day after the opening date as day 1, and the lapse is due when the current date is on or after the opening date plus 30 calendar days. The opening date carried on the account record is the anchor, and the comparison is not-earlier-than, so the day the window is reached itself satisfies it.

### 6. The promotional end date

For a tier that offers a promotional annual percentage yield, a promotional end date is recorded at opening as the opening date plus the tier's promotional duration in calendar months, falling back to the last day of the month where that day does not exist in the closing month.

### Boundary of the funding window

Take a hypothetical account opened on 3 March and still in applied status. Day 1 of the window is 4 March, and the opening date plus 30 calendar days falls on 2 April. On 1 April the window has not been reached and the account has not lapsed. On 2 April it has been reached and the lapse is due; on 3 April it is due likewise, the comparison being on or after.
